title: How a Sewing Machine Works in 60 Seconds 🧵🪡 #shorts
description:
A sewing machine doesn't sew like a hand. It ties two threads together: the needle pushes a loop of top thread through the fabric, a spinning hook swings that loop around the bobbin, and a lever pulls the knot tight inside the cloth. Follow Inside 60 for a new "how it works" explained in 60 seconds.

#sewingmachine #sewing #howitworks

steps.label: Hook
steps.text: Industrial sewing machines can make about *5,000 stitches* every minute.

steps.label: Two threads
steps.text: Every stitch uses *two threads*: one from the top spool, and one from a small *bobbin* below.

steps.label: Needle
steps.text: The *needle* pushes the top thread through the fabric, then rises a little to open a *loop*.

steps.label: Spinning hook
steps.text: A spinning *hook* grabs that loop and swings it all the way around the *bobbin*.

steps.label: Lock
steps.text: The *take-up lever* pulls the thread tight, locking both threads inside the fabric.

steps.label: Feed
steps.text: Then little toothed *feed dogs* push the fabric forward for the *next stitch*.

steps.label: Recap
steps.text: Loop, hook, *lock*. Follow Inside 60 for more.
